contract:
# Named type metadata revisit

Outcome: classify immutable named type declarations once and reuse positive request-owned class IDs across parameter, return and property checks. Baseline 929df6ed is clean, source 9635606606194d209de413515955f5159194a1edbf5f456b3b96dff7a080c967; accepted PGO analysis uses 74.2814G versus PHP 10.3374G. Current exact Callgrind type-check budget is 2.1598G inclusive, including 0.7459G target lookup. Prior independent prototype removed ~1G instructions but was rejected under the superseded time-led tradeoff criterion.

Hypothesis: stable declaration metadata removes repeated named-kind comparisons and successful target hashing. Restore the prior generic TypeName representation, adapt the current lazy lexical/called scope API, use never-reused executor identity and positive-only cache; no workload recognizer. Sole integrator owns affected type/runtime/compiler/stdlib files.

Semantics: misses observe later declarations and aliases; self/parent/static follow current lexical/called scopes and are never globally cached. Preserve exact spelling/equality/reflection, unions/intersections, COW and all errors. Reused/shared hints across moved or different executors cannot reuse a different request's class IDs. Unregistered class-zero receivers retain canonical name checks. No unsafe additions.

Gates: existing named-cache identity/alias tests, type/coercion/property/relative closure tests, exact PHP differentials, native phase comparison against identical opt-level-one baseline as an early diagnostic, then independent PGO and instruction confirmation, default/no-default/all-feature focused gates, all-target check, independent controls and cleanup. The early opt-level-one comparison cannot establish a PGO saving. Stop before broad verification if it increases instructions or changes output; fresh PGO must show reproducible reduction at least 0.5% to earn production adoption. Keep time/RSS/regressions visible under user instruction priority. Do not alter unsafe ceiling.
